To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified five genes, PMEPA1, LAPTM4α, SLC25A1, LITAF and CYYR1, that increase both intracellular glutathi-one levels and [3h]glutathione uptake rates.
we identified five PY-containing proteins that increase glutathione and endocytotic marker uptake in yeast cells.

(i) five genes were identified in a yeast screen that complement a GSH uptake defect in a yeast mutant; (ii) all five genes encode integral membrane proteins; (iii) all five genes enhance both GSH uptake and uptake of endocytotic marker dyes in yeast; (iv) all five genes contain PY motifs; and (v) mutation of the PY motif in LITAF abolishes all of its effects in yeast.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of genes that are involved in the uptake of glutathione (γ-Glu-Cys-Gly; GSH) into mammalian cells.
the identification and characterization of proteins that regulate the uptake and efflux of GSH in mammalian cells.
the transport and cellular functions of GSH and related compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the five genes identified are involved in GSH transport and endocytotic marker uptake, although none are prototypical GSH or endocytotic transporters.
the results do not identify novel GSH transport proteins, but do identify five novel human proteins containing PY motifs that may influence membrane transport.

the five human gene products that are capable of enhancing GSH uptake in the yeast Hgt1p-deficient strain, and which contain PY motifs, are not GSH transporters per se, but may influence GSH transport activity by affecting the cell surface expression of other GSH transporters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified 5 PY containing genes, 2 of which are known to have roles in endocytosis.
we have identified 5 human proteins that contain a PY motif and that enhance GSH and endocytotic marker uptake in yeast cells.
the PY motifs of the proteins we identified appear to be involved in regulating the plasma membrane transport activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PY motif may be involved in regulating GSH transport activity in mammalian cells.
the PY motifs may play an important role in regulating membrane transporter activity.

the PY motif appears to be important for the function of a variety of proteins, and that it may be possible to identify PY motif-containing proteins involved in GSH transport by screening for PY mutants that lose GSH transport activity.
